Francisci, e Pola, camini scopator», mother «Clagnan Dominica, Angeli, e Pola», godfather Voltolina Antonius, carpenter, with Nardin Eduardus as witness** ([image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-R9MZ?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-3YS)). `doc`. **A marginal note added later reads «uxorem duxit Annam Zulian[i], Polae 31.X.1920»** — he married at Pola on 31 October 1920 (`doc` for the note; the bride's surname is read at one construction only and is doubtful). **A Pola-born family from a Gračišće one: the father is «gn Francisci e Pola» — and his father Franciscus, buried at Pula in 1875, is «fil. Two deaths in one line. «*della fu*» puts the mother in the ground already; «*fu Pietro*» puts her father there too. So **Michiela De Franceschi, daughter of a Pietro, was dead before January 1831** — and this archive would never have heard of her at all if her daughter had not died young enough to need her named. A **sixth** woman who left the surname and came back only through a child.

children.name: Josephus Aloysius de Franceschi
children.note: **In no index anywhere.** Almost certainly the **Giuseppe × Francesca** who heads the Rijeka chain — right forename, right town, and **twenty-four** at his first child's baptism in November 1772.

confirmed: One baptism, read on the page. The household is documented; its extent is not.
read:
**Found by reading, not by searching** — film 005497925, image 150, 20 September 2026, during a frame-by-frame sweep of the 1746–1750 gap. **This is the second Defranceschi household at Fiume**, beside Valentino the Carnian's, and this archive did not know it existed.

**Only one child is known**, because only one page has been read. **Magdalena was dead by December 1771**, when Joannes Baptista remarries as a widower to **Catharina de Benzoni**; he has indexed children by her in 1773 and 1776. **No marriage of his stands in the Fiume register between 1736 and 1748**, all of which has been read — so he married elsewhere, and **Magdalena's maiden name is the open question**. See [the second household](/fiume-1626/#jbaptista).

confirmed: Both parents named together in the baptisms of their children, 1769–1778, and the father styled **D.no** each time.
read: «**Fran.ca figlia di D.no Ant.o De Franceschi** e Donna **Mattia** … nata li 8 corrente» (9 December 1769), and «**Dom[ini]cus filius leg[iti]mus Antonij Defranceschi, Matthiae ejus uxoris, natus die 25 elapsi mensis**» (2 January 1778). Both magnified. Antonio is the parish **campanaro** — the bell-ringer — which is why his name fills the witness lines of the 1770s. **Vittorio is placed here on a burial, not a baptism**: buried 8 November 1812 aged 54, *kin: Antonio*, and called «*Victorius filius Antonii de Franceschi*» in the register in 1773, 1782 and 1787. **Maria has no baptism in this volume at all** — she is here because two entries call her «*Maria filia Antonii de Franceschi ex hac Parochia*» (1786, 1787). Her birth is therefore undated, and frames 5–60 covering 1764–1775 do not contain it.

confirmed: Five baptisms across seventeen years naming the same couple, and a joint godparent line of 29 April 1753 naming them together; the father dead before November 1771, and the mother remarried on 22 October 1765 as «Pasqua Ved.a q.m Giacomo de Franceschi». The eldest child was moved here from [h113] on 28 September 2026 when his mother's name was re-read.
read:
Read on the leaf at images 155, 163, 169 and 179 of the 1709–1764 volume, each magnified. **The eldest child's forename could not be recovered** — the leaf is flagged *razlivena tinta*, run ink, and would not resolve even at full plate scale; the parents were legible and the given name was not. It is carried here as a child without a name rather than dropped, because the act exists and the household is one child larger than its names suggest.

**Two things about this couple are unresolved and are not smoothed over here.** Godmothers styled «*uxor Jacobi Defranceschi*» are read as **Veneranda** in 1754, 1755 and 1756, while these four baptisms give the mother as **Pascasia** — so either two Giacomos ran at once or one of the readings is wrong; neither has been magnified. And on 12 May 1754 a godfather is «*Jacobus filius Jacobi Defranceschi*», an adult son of a Giacomo nine months after Giacomo Battista was born. **Two generations of the forename existed before 1754**, which is why the groom of 1772 is not merged with the child of 1753.

**23 September 2026 — this household begins four years earlier than recorded, and its husband is now distinguishable from the parish's other Giacomo.**

**31 March 1746**: *«**Martina Antonia filia legitima Jacobi Defranceschi, et Pascasia ejus legitima uxoris amborum ex hac Parochia**, nata 28 currentis»*, godfather **D.nus Martinus Peispach ex Dignano** — **Martina Antonia di Jacobo Defranceschi 1746**, read on image 143 and magnified.

**Pascasia is now attested as a mother in a full parental entry**, which matters because the other Giacomo's wife, **Francisca Marcario**, is attested the same way in **1743** ([h113]). *Two baptisms, two mothers, one forename, three years apart — and their godparental appearances interleave across the same years rather than succeeding one another, seven days apart in the winter of 1743.* **Two contemporary men, not one who remarried.** *(doc for the act; the separation is inf.)*

**A second child, and a name repeated.** **27 October 1747**: *«**Antonia filia legitima Jacobi Defranceschi, et Pascasia ejus legitima uxoris amborum ex hac Parochia**, nata die 20 currentis»* — **Antonia di Jacobo Defranceschi 1747**, godparents **D.us Joannes Baptista Legiani** and **D.us Faustinus, son of the chancellor Francesco Saverio Profumo**.

**⚠ Nineteen months after Martina *Antonia*, and the name is the same.** *A parish does not give one living daughter's name to the next.* **The elder almost certainly died in infancy.** The burial register for these years has not been read. *(doc for both baptisms; the death is inf, on the naming alone.)*

**27 September 2026 — the child of 25 March 1750 has her name.** *«**Victoria filia legitima Jacobi Defranceschi, ac Pascasia ejus legitima uxoris, amborum ex hac Parochia, nata hodie**»*, godparents **Paulus Venier** and **Euphemia uxor Natalis Zanzevin** — **[Victoria di Jacobo Defranceschi (1750)](/person/victoria-di-jacobo-defranceschi-1750/)**. *This household has carried her since long before as «[forename not read]», the date right and the word missing.* **The plate supplies it, and nothing new was invented to do so.**

**And Pascasia's marriage is now proved the way Jacoba's is.** **29 April 1753**: *«patrini fuerunt, **Jacobus Defranceschi, et Pascasia ejus uxor**»* — the two of them in one phrase. *Which convicts the two entries calling her «uxor Caspari» in December 1751 and February 1752 as the clerk writing the wrong husband, twice, for one woman.*

**28 September 2026 — this household begins in 1743, not 1746.** *The baptism of **Casparus**, 1 June 1743, was filed under [h113] because his mother was read as «Francisca». **She is Pascasia** — proved against the same clerk's «Franciscus» on the facing leaf and his own «Pascasia» on image 143. See [/corrections/](/corrections/).* **Casparus is this household's eldest child**, and the run is 1743–1759, six children over sixteen years.

confirmed: The father named again twenty-five years later, at the son's own appearance as godfather.
read:
The index gives «*Casparg, of **Jacobo De Franceschi and Anzola**, 26 December 1737*». The register then confirms the descent twice in 1762: «*padrini furono **Gasparo figlio di M.o Giacomo de Franceschi***»* on 1 August and again on 15 December — magnified. Gasparo is twenty-four in 1762, which is exactly what the 1737 baptism predicts. **Giacomo therefore married twice**: Anzola, who bore Gasparo in 1737, and Pascasia, whose four children run 1750–1759.

Gasparo was **dead before 30 March 1773**, when «*Maria relicta q.m Gasparis de Franceschi*» remarried.

**23 September 2026 — the register gives him a twin.** Image 116 of the same volume: *«baptizavit **duos infantulos geminos natos hodie mane a Jacobo de Franceschi, et Anzola ejus legitima uxore ambobus ex hac Parochia**, quibus fuit positum nomen, uni [Gasparo] alteri **Antonij**»*. **The index's «Casparg» is one of two boys born that morning**, and the second is **Antonio**. *The forename this archive could not read off the plate is supplied by the index line already on this row — each source answering the other's gap.*

confirmed: Their marriage found: 10 June 1772, «Giacobus filius Giacobi de Franceschi et Nicolina filia Nicolai Teserati».
read: **This is the first household at this parish joined to its own wedding from two read acts rather than an index line.** The marriage register has the couple on **10 June 1772**; the first child arrives eighteen months later — «*Adi 22 Xbre 1773. **Pasqua e Vitoria figlia di Giacomo de Franceschi, e di Nicoletta** jugali, **nata li 16***»* — and the second on **3 March 1778**, «*Joannes filius leg[itim]us Jacobi Defranceschi et Nicolae ejus uxoris, natus heri die*». Both magnified. **Nicolina and Nicoletta are one woman**, the clerk writing the same name two ways.

confirmed: The wife named in full in the register itself, five times between 1785 and 1791, as «Euphemia uxor Victorii de Franceschi».
read:
«*Anno Dni 1784 Die 4 Septembris. **Maria Matthia filia legitima, ac naturalis Victorii, et Euphemiæ jugalium De Franceschi**, nata 3 currentis*». Magnified. **This act was read past once.** The frame-by-frame sweep of the volume missed it; it was recovered by resolving the FamilySearch index entry's own image ark, which pointed back at a frame already read. The marriage had until then rested on that index line alone.

**Four more children are held out of this household deliberately.** The burial register names Vittorio as kin to **Antonia** (born 1804, died aged 4), **Giovanni Pietro** (1809), **Antonio** (1811) and **Gioanni Maria** (died June 1813). **No mother is named in any of them**, and twenty years separate them from Maria Matthia. They are Vittorio's children on the register's word; they are not recorded here as Euphemia's, and the volume covering 1792–1803 has not been read.

confirmed: The wife named as his four times across five years, in four separate entries.
read:
«*a **Petro de Franceschi**, et **Jacoba** ejus legitima uxore **ambobus ex hac Parochia***» — **27 July 1738**, baptising **Anna Euphemia**, born the 25th. Godparents **Blasius Marsoni**, smith, and **D.na Margarita**.

**Jacoba is his wife five times over**: as a parent here, and as a godmother on **29 December 1739**, **16 February 1742**, **29 June 1743** and **3 May 1744**, each time *«uxor Petri Defranceschi»* — the last of them read on image 137 and magnified. **Six years of one marriage, in a parish where the register gives Jacobo three wives in eight days.** *That contrast is the point: the clerk is not careless, and where he repeats a pairing he means it.*

**The second child is inferred, not read as his.** On **4 October 1739** the register baptises **Euphemia**, *«a **Batta** Defranceschi et **Jacoba** ejus legitima uxore»* — the same mother's name, the same daughter's name, fourteen months later, and **a different father's forename**. *Three entries put Jacoba with Pietro and one puts her with a Batta, and the Batta entry sits between two of them.* **The likeliest reading is that the first Euphemia died and the name was given again**, and that the clerk wrote the wrong husband. *(doc for Anna Euphemia; **inf** for Euphemia, and the entry has not been altered — it still reads* Batta *under magnification.)*

**A third child, and the one that makes this a household rather than an episode.** **14 February 1745**: *«**Valentinus filius legitimus Petri Defranceschi, et Jacoba ejus legitima uxoris, ambobus ex hac Parochia**, natus die 11 currentis»* — godfather **Antonius Valentinus Colovri ex Cargno**, who gives the boy his name. **Valentino di Pietro Defranceschi 1745**. *(doc.)* **Seven years of Pietro and Jacoba, 1738 to 1745**, across two baptisms of their own and five godparent lines.

**A fourth child, and the entry that removes every remaining doubt about this couple.** **10 February 1746**: *«**Victoria filia Petri Defranceschi, et Jacoba ejus legitima uxoris amborum ex hac Parochia**, nata die 1mo currentis»* — **Victoria di Pietro Defranceschi 1746**, godfather **Joannes Clozo faber**.

**And four months earlier the two of them stand at a font together.** **10 October 1745**: *«patrini ad Sacrum Fontem fuerunt, **Petrus Defranceschi, et Jacoba ejus uxor**»* — *husband and wife named in one line, in one hand, with no room for the clerk to attach her to the wrong man.* **Eight years, four children and seven joint appearances.** *(doc.)*

**And once more, 22 May 1746**: *«Patrini fuerunt ad Sacrum Fontem, Natalis Zanzevin, ac **Jacoba uxor Petri Defranceschi**»* — her seventh appearance in that formula, over eight years, always with the same husband. *(doc.)*

**Three more, and they run past the last child.** *«Jacoba uxor Petri Defranceschi»* stands godmother on **13 December 1746** (image 145), **3 May 1747** (image 146) and **9 October 1747** (image 147) — her **eighth, ninth and tenth** appearances in that formula. **Ten times across ten years, one husband, never another.** *(doc.)*

**A fifth child, and a name used for the third time.** **17 September 1749**: *«**Euphemia filia Petri Defranceschi, et Jacoba ejus legitima uxoris, amborum ex hac Parochia**, nata hodie»* — **Euphemia di Pietro Defranceschi 1749**, *baptised the day she was born*, godfather **Faustino, son of the late Joannes Baptista Defranceschi**.

**⚠ Anna Euphemia (1738), Euphemia (1739), Euphemia (1749).** *A parish does not give one living daughter's name to two of her sisters.* **The first two almost certainly died small.** The burial register has not been read. *(doc for the baptisms; inf for the deaths.)*

confirmed: Both parents named in full on both baptisms, and the wife named again as a godmother between them. A fifth daughter, Fusca, is added from her marriage of 17 November 1773 — «Fusca filia q. Mathiæ de Franceschi» — tied to this household by the witness Mathias Santalezza, the surname Helena married into in 1766. No baptism of hers has been found.
read:
**Eleven years of one household, entirely inside the stretch the index does not cover.**

· **27 August 1741** — *«**Francisca uxor Matthei Defranceschi**»* stands godmother, which is the couple's earliest appearance.
· **10 August 1742** — *«natam die 5 currentis **a Matthæo Defranceschi, et Francisca ejus legitima uxore ambobus ex hac Parochia**, cui positum fuit nomen **Helena**»*, godparent **Martinus Stancovich**.
· **15 February 1752** — *«**Irena filia legitima Matthæi Defranceschi, et Francisca ejus legitimæ uxoris ambo ex hac Parochia**, nata die 11 currentis»*, godparents **Zorzi (?) Lanich** and **Maria, wife of Joannes Valentich**.

*Both parents are «of this parish» on both acts, so neither is an incomer.* **doc.**

**A middle child, and it closes the gap.** **28 October 1745**: *«**Maria filia Matthæi Defranceschi, et Francisca ejus legitima uxoris amborum ex hac Parochia**, nata die 15 currentis»*, godparents **Dominicus Diasich ex Dignano** and **Elena uxor Joanis Filipich ex Fasano** — *both from outside the parish*. **Maria di Matteo Defranceschi 1745**. **Matteo himself stands godfather three weeks later**, on **17 November 1745**. *(doc.)*

**A fourth child.** **21 September 1749**: *«**Victoria filia Matthei Defranceschi, et Francisca ejus legitima uxoris, amborum ex hac Parochia**, nata die 19 currentis»* — **Victoria di Matteo Defranceschi 1749**. **Francesca is named his wife again on 21 January 1748**, and **Matteo stands godfather on 14 March 1748 and 25 September 1749**. *Eight years of one household, unbroken.* *(doc.)*

father: Giacomo de Franceschi (husband of Francisca Marcario)
confirmed: No baptism. This household rests entirely on four godparent lines naming a «Francisca / Franca Marcario, uxor Jacobi Defranceschi» — 1 December 1743, 26 March and 17 December 1752, and 6 February 1753.
read:
**⚠ This household had one child until 28 September 2026, and he was never hers.**

*It was built on the baptism of **Casparus**, 1 June 1743, whose mother the archive read as «**Francisca**». **She is Pascasia** — the same word the clerk writes on image 143 for [h107]'s mother, stroke for stroke, and sharing two letters with his own «Franciscus» on the facing leaf. **Casparus has been moved to [h107]**, and this household is left with no baptism at all.* See [/corrections/](/corrections/).

**What remains is four godparent lines** — *«[Franca] Mar-/:cario uxor Jacobi Defranceschi» (1 December 1743), «Franca Marcario uxor Jacobi Defranceschi» (26 March 1752), «Francisca uxor Jacobi Defranceschi» (17 December 1752) and the same on 6 February 1753.* **A godparent line is the weakest object in this volume**, and this archive has twice convicted one of naming the wrong husband. *The household is kept because the woman is attested four times over ten years, which is not a slip of the pen — but it is **a wife without a child**, and the page should say so.* **(inf.)**

confirmed: Both parents named in full on both baptisms of the town register.
read:
**A carpenter's household at Parenzo, and a marquis at the font.**

· **11 November 1844** — **Anna Maria**, born 20 October, father *«**Matteo Defranceschi, falegname**»*, mother **Domenica Frezza**; midwife **Elena Weber**.
· **«Parenzo li 28 Luglio 1846.** **Paolo Francesco Domenico** figlio delli giugali **Mattio Defranceschi falegn.** e **Domenica Frezza** nacque li 26 corr.» — baptised by Canon **Pietro Monfalcon**, godparents **Francesco Marchese de Polesini** and **Ellena de Filippini-Coletti**.

**The Polesini were the first noble house of Parenzo**, and a marquis of that family stood for a carpenter's son.

*Anna Maria is very probably the **«Anna Maria Defranceschi, moglie di Giacomo Rocco»** who dies in the same town on 17 September 1879 aged thirty-five — the arithmetic is exact.* **(doc for both baptisms; inf for the death.)** Film 005497830, images 62 and 309.

confirmed: Both parents named in full on the baptism, both «of this parish».
read:
**A household that existed only behind a loose piece of paper.**

«**Die 13 Junij, 1745. Antonia filia Victorij Defranceschi, et Dominica ejus legitima Uxoris amborum ex hac Parochia, nata die 12 currentis**, baptizata fuit a R.do D.no **Antonio Stancovich** Canc.: Patrini fuerunt, Vincentius Bracovich, et **Elena vidua defuncti Blasij Marsoni**.»

**On image 140 this page is covered by a slip** — an Italian memorandum recording the baptism of the castle **chancellor's** own daughter, with **Paolo Manzini, Captain of this Castle**, at the font. **Image 141 is the same opening photographed again with the slip lifted.** *The register's duplicate frames are not redundancy; they are the only way some entries are visible at all.*

**The father is Vittorio Defranceschi Godfather 1744**, who stands godfather to a foundling on 5 June 1744 — *not* the Vittorio born about 1758 who witnesses from 1773 and whom this archive has long carried. **A man with a baptised child in 1745 is not a man born in 1758.** The later Vittorio is very probably his grandson. *(doc for the act; the two Vittorios are inf but not close.)*

**The godmother ties the household to Pietro's.** *Blasius Marsoni, smith*, was godfather to **Anna Euphemia di Pietro Defranceschi** on 27 July 1738; by June 1745 he is dead and his widow **Elena** stands in his place.

**Twins, three years later.** «**Die 10. Februarij, 1748. Lucia, et Dominicus filii gemini Victorij Defranceschi, et Dominica ejus legitima uxoris, amborum ex hac Parochia, nati nocte elapsa**» — **Lucia di Vittorio Defranceschi, twin 1748** and **Dominico di Vittorio Defranceschi, twin 1748**, each given its own pair of godparents, hers **Joannes Baptista Miceij ex Castro** and **Michaelis Valentich**, his **D.us Jacobus Zuecha, surgeon**, and **Joannes Jedreicich**. *(doc.)*

read: **Johann Defranceschi, navy servant of the 4th class, born at Gračišće, married Paula Pietra, 19, born at Pola, on 16 January 1871** — the entry names his parents as «Franz Defranceschi, Besitzer» and **Franziska née Salomon** ([the entry](/person/johann-joannes-defranceschi-navy-servant-1833/); `doc`). *He is, `inf`, the brother of the Franciscus of [h129](/households/) and the son of [h116](/households/); his father is written Franz where the Gračišće and Pula civil books have Joannes Baptista.* His wife's father is Rocco …, her mother Johanna Borri. **Five children are known, all born at Pola and all baptised in the naval parish, the mother written «Paula Petra, daughter of Peter Rocco»:** **Raimund Johann**, born 19 October 1871, baptised 12 November — a later note says he married on 21 December 1927 in a parish of S. Ant. Taum. (Trieste?) to «Sofia Kiroly» (naval baptisms, 9R2C-K68 image 182; `doc`); **Peter Nicolaus**, born 14 March 1874, baptised 10 May — `inf` the «Anton» of the death book, who died of convulsions on 2 October 1874, aged 7 months (9R2C-K68 image 247 and the naval deaths 9R2C-7MW image 247; the two forenames are unreconciled); **Eugen Josef**, born 8 December 1875, baptised 26 February 1876, died 10 November 1890, aged 14, of a fractured skull (9R2C-K68 image 292; naval deaths 9R28-N35 image 92; `doc`); **Francisca Antonia**, born 24 January 1878, baptised 17 September, died of diphtheria on 4 August 1882, aged 4½ — seven months before her mother (9R2Z-K6L image 63; naval hospital deaths 9R28-FMQ image 77; `doc`); and **Johann Carl**, born 2 April 1881, baptised 19 April — a note records his marriage to Ida Revelant in the Pola cathedral on 10 July 1911 (9R2Z-K6L image 147; `doc`). **Paula died at Pola on 27 February 1883**, aged 31½, of lung tuberculosis, in the civil hospital, and was buried on the naval cemetery on 1 March; her husband is then «k.k. Marine-Diener 2. Cl.» (naval deaths, 9R28-6YS image 105; `doc`). Three of the five children died young; Raimund Johann and Johann Carl are the two who grew up. Johann's own death is not found.
